page_title: The traits of a proficient programmer

sources.entry: The traits of a proficient programmer

summary.title: The traits of a proficient programmer
summary.one_liner: Proficiency means knowing why you do things a certain way and how the parts fit the whole, which is the step beyond competence that many developers get stuck on.
keywords: fit the tool to the job
how to become a better programmer
takeaways: Competence means knowing how to get things done; proficiency means knowing why you do them and how they fit the big picture.
Design patterns applied without big-picture understanding are often used inappropriately; a proficient programmer recognizes when a pattern breaks down or is irrelevant.
Treat patterns, principles, libraries and language features as tools and fit the tool to the job.
Practical ways to build proficiency include reasoning from the current problem, learning fewer things more deeply, reading primary sources, and working in unfamiliar projects.
Ask others for examples and context rather than accepting dogmatic reasoning.
summary.summary: The article contrasts competence (knowing how to do things) with proficiency (understanding why things are done a certain way and how the parts fit together). It uses the Dreyfus Model of Skill Acquisition as background and illustrates the difference with the Memento design pattern, showing how a competent programmer may misapply it while a proficient one spots its limits and adapts it. It closes with a list of exercises for building proficiency, such as reasoning from context, breaking rules deliberately, and going deep on a narrow skill.
